question.problem:
A bouquet consists of $20$ roses. The weight of a rose, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $70\,\text{g}$ and a standard deviation of $5\,\text{g}.$ If one bouquet is randomly selected, what is the probability that it will weigh more than $1\,430\,\text{g}?$ You may assume that the weights of the roses in a bouquet are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8925\,$ | $\,0.8944\,$ | $\,0.8962\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9099\,$ | $\,0.9115\,$ | $\,0.9131\,$ | $\,0.9147\,$ |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9251\,$ | $\,0.9265\,$ | $\,0.9279\,$ | $\,0.9292\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{i}$ denote the weight of the $i$th rose. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(70,{5}^{2}),\,1\le i\le 20.
$$

Let the random variable $W$ denote the weight of a randomly selected bouquet. Then, since

$$
W={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+⋯+{X}_{20},
$$

we have that $W$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =20\cdot 70 \\  & =1\,400, \\ \text{Var}[W] & =20\cdot {5}^{2} \\  & =500.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
W∼N(1\,400,500).
$$

In order to find $P(W>1\,430),$ we convert $W$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W>1\,430) & =P(Z>\frac{1\,430-1\,400}{\sqrt{500}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>1.34) \\  & =1-P(Z<1.34) \\  & =1-Φ(1.34)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(1.34)≈0.9099.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W>1\,430) & ≈1-Φ(1.34) \\  & ≈0.0901.\end{aligned}
$$
